reference_prolog:
/*  Self-contained SWI-Prolog program (Georgia, 2021)

    Question: Can a landlord evict a tenant for committing substantial damage to the property?

    Statutes encoded:
      - GA Code  44-7-10 (2021)  (surrender possession at end of term; summary remedy for holding over)
      - GA Code  44-7-50 (2021)  (demand for possession; dispossessory affidavit for certain grounds)
      - GA Code  44-7-24 (2021)  (retaliation defense; exceptions including intentional property damage)
*/

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
%% Basic domain predicates (parties, relationships, and properties)
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%

% Parties and property in this scenario.
landlord(l1).
tenant(t1).
premises(p1).

% Landlord-tenant relationship must exist for summary eviction proceedings.
% (Judicial decision note under GA Code  44-7-10 references requirement.)
landlord_tenant_relationship(l1, t1, p1).

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
%% Scenario facts (encode the question's factual statement)
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%

/* The question fact pattern: tenant committed substantial damage to the property.
   The statutes provided explicitly reference "intentionally damages property"
   (GA Code  44-7-24(d)(2)). To connect the question to the statute text,
   we model "committing substantial damage" as intentional damage to the premises.
*/
substantial_damage_by_tenant(t1, p1).

% Interpretation/bridge for applying GA Code  44-7-24(d)(2):
% committing substantial damage is treated as intentional property damage.
intentional_property_damage_by_tenant(Tenant, Premises) :-
    substantial_damage_by_tenant(Tenant, Premises).

/* Helper predicate required by the prompt:
   Succeeds when the factual statement scenario is satisfied. */
scenario_statement :-
    tenant(T),
    premises(P),
    substantial_damage_by_tenant(T, P).

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
%% Statute translations (deterministic "statute_*" predicates)
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%

/* GA Code  44-7-10 (2021)
   Tenant must deliver possession at expiration of term; if fails, summary remedy.
   (We encode the "holding over after term expiration" concept.)
*/
statute_ga_44_7_10_summary_remedy_available(Landlord, Tenant, Premises) :-
    landlord_tenant_relationship(Landlord, Tenant, Premises),
    lease_expired(Landlord, Tenant, Premises),
    tenant_failed_to_deliver_possession(Landlord, Tenant, Premises).

/* GA Code  44-7-50 (2021)
   Owner may demand possession when:
     (a) tenant holds over beyond term, OR
     (b) tenant fails to pay rent when due, OR
     (c) property held by tenant at will or sufferance.
   If tenant refuses/fails to deliver possession after demand, owner may file affidavit
   (start dispossessory process).
*/
statute_ga_44_7_50_ground_holding_over(Landlord, Tenant, Premises) :-
    landlord_tenant_relationship(Landlord, Tenant, Premises),
    tenant_holds_over_beyond_term(Landlord, Tenant, Premises).

statute_ga_44_7_50_ground_nonpayment(Landlord, Tenant, Premises) :-
    landlord_tenant_relationship(Landlord, Tenant, Premises),
    rent_due_and_unpaid(Landlord, Tenant, Premises).

statute_ga_44_7_50_ground_at_will_or_sufferance(Landlord, Tenant, Premises) :-
    landlord_tenant_relationship(Landlord, Tenant, Premises),
    tenant_at_will_or_sufferance(Landlord, Tenant, Premises).

statute_ga_44_7_50_demand_and_refusal_allows_affidavit(Landlord, Tenant, Premises) :-
    (   statute_ga_44_7_50_ground_holding_over(Landlord, Tenant, Premises)
    ;   statute_ga_44_7_50_ground_nonpayment(Landlord, Tenant, Premises)
    ;   statute_ga_44_7_50_ground_at_will_or_sufferance(Landlord, Tenant, Premises)
    ),
    owner_demands_possession(Landlord, Tenant, Premises),
    tenant_refuses_or_fails_to_deliver_after_demand(Landlord, Tenant, Premises).

/* GA Code  44-7-24 (2021) retaliation defense and exceptions.
   Key exception for this question:
      44-7-24(d)(2): landlord not liable for retaliation (and thus may proceed
     "in accordance with this chapter") when the tenant intentionally damages
     property on the premises.
   We encode that "intentional property damage" is a statutorily recognized basis
   for dispossessory/termination not barred as retaliation.
*/
statute_ga_44_7_24_exception_intentional_damage_applies(Landlord, Tenant, Premises) :-
    landlord_tenant_relationship(Landlord, Tenant, Premises),
    intentional_property_damage_by_tenant(Tenant, Premises),
    landlord(Landlord).

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
%% Additional legal reasoning helpers (apply statutes to scenario)
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%

/* A "legal ground" for eviction/dispossessory under the provided statutes.
   - Holding over / nonpayment / at-will-or-sufferance are explicit in  44-7-50.
   - Intentional property damage is treated as a permitted basis via  44-7-24(d)(2)
     (exception to retaliation liability; indicates the chapter contemplates this basis).
*/
legal_ground_for_eviction(Landlord, Tenant, Premises, holding_over) :-
    statute_ga_44_7_50_ground_holding_over(Landlord, Tenant, Premises).

legal_ground_for_eviction(Landlord, Tenant, Premises, nonpayment) :-
    statute_ga_44_7_50_ground_nonpayment(Landlord, Tenant, Premises).

legal_ground_for_eviction(Landlord, Tenant, Premises, at_will_or_sufferance) :-
    statute_ga_44_7_50_ground_at_will_or_sufferance(Landlord, Tenant, Premises).

legal_ground_for_eviction(Landlord, Tenant, Premises, intentional_property_damage) :-
    statute_ga_44_7_24_exception_intentional_damage_applies(Landlord, Tenant, Premises).

/* "Can evict" for this QA is modeled as: landlord has a legally recognized ground
   (among those encoded from the provided statutes) to pursue dispossessory/eviction.
*/
landlord_may_evict(Landlord, Tenant, Premises) :-
    legal_ground_for_eviction(Landlord, Tenant, Premises, _Ground).

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
%% Facts NOT present in the question (kept false by omission)
%% We include these predicates so the program is complete and compiles,
%% but we do not assert any such facts for this scenario.
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%

% Lease end / holding over / possession demand facts (not alleged in the question).
lease_expired(_Landlord, _Tenant, _Premises) :- fail.
tenant_failed_to_deliver_possession(_Landlord, _Tenant, _Premises) :- fail.
tenant_holds_over_beyond_term(_Landlord, _Tenant, _Premises) :- fail.

% Rent nonpayment facts (not alleged).
rent_due_and_unpaid(_Landlord, _Tenant, _Premises) :- fail.

% Tenancy at will or sufferance facts (not alleged).
tenant_at_will_or_sufferance(_Landlord, _Tenant, _Premises) :- fail.

% Demand/refusal procedural facts (not alleged).
owner_demands_possession(_Landlord, _Tenant, _Premises) :- fail.
tenant_refuses_or_fails_to_deliver_after_demand(_Landlord, _Tenant, _Premises) :- fail.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
%% Final answer predicate (deterministic yes/no)
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%

housing_answer(yes) :-
    scenario_statement,
    landlord_may_evict(l1, t1, p1),
    !.
housing_answer(no) :-
    scenario_statement,
    !.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
%% Main entrypoint (required)
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%

main :-
    housing_answer(Result),
    format('housing_answer(~w).~n', [Result]).


:- initialization(main, main).

expected.question: Can a landlord evict a tenant for commiting substantial damage to the property?
